previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease and a complex medical history, including lupus, anticardiolipin antibody syndrome, and prior transplant failure, was admitted for laparoscopic placement of a peritoneal dialysis catheter with lysis of adhesions. Postoperatively, she developed a transient fever managed with Levaquin, and a slow drop in hematocrit prompted a single unit red blood cell transfusion. The catheter site showed bloody effluent initially but cleared with daily flushes. A telemetry alarm suggesting ventricular fibrillation was determined to be artifactual by cardiology. She remained afebrile by hospital day 4, tolerated oral intake, ambulated well, and was discharged home in stable condition. She will follow up with the PD nurse for training and continue hemodialysis in the interim. Warfarin was restarted at a reduced dose with close INR monitoring.
